verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling unwell for four days with sore throat, runny nose, congestion, new dry cough since yesterday, and feeling tired: "under the weather for the past four days", "started with the... sore throat and runny nose", "it's sort of going into a cough now... starting to cough", "that started recently... maybe yesterday... it's dry", and "kind of... bad and tired."

Patient states exposure to a sick colleague whose children are in kindergarten: "this colleague of mine, she just kept sneezing next to me... I think her kids are catching something from their kindergarten or something."

Patient describes initial fever improved with paracetamol and ibuprofen: "I had some some fever in the beginning, but it's now sort of going down. I've been taking some Paracetamol and Ibuprofen for that, and they help."

Patient reports night sweats for same time frame as other symptoms: "I'm also having uh night sweats" and doctor confirms timing: "this has again, been going on for last uh three four days, has it?" Patient replies, "Yeah, yes."

Cough is dry and constant without time-of-day variation: "it's dry for now", "it's sort of there, all the time" and in response to diurnal variation question, patient says, "No it's it's um, it's sort of, it's sort of constant."

Patient had painful swallowing 1–2 days; no exudate observed by patient; no ear pain or discharge: "it was quite painful to swallow, for one or two days"; "You didn't notice any abnormal white spots, redness at the back of your throat?" Patient: "No"; "Any pain in, in your ears at all?" Patient: "Um no" and "you don't feel blocked, or any discharge coming out of your ears?" Patient: "No, I don't think so."

No chest pain and exertional dyspnea only, none at rest: "so no pain in chest" and "I feel a bit winded on exertion" and doctor clarifies "that's mainly on exercise. But when you're resting, there's no problem." Patient: "Yeah, yeah. When when when I'm resting it's OK."

Intermittent generalized headaches without visual changes or photophobia: "any headaches at all?" Patient: "yeah..."; "Whereabouts... ?" Patient: "it's sort of general... they're not always there, but... come and go."; "with those headaches have you had any problems with your... vision?" Patient: "Um no."; "any difficulty with seeing bright lights?" Patient: "No, I don't think so."

No nausea or vomiting and normal bowels and urine: "any feeling nausea or any vomiting?" Patient: "No, none of that."; "Tell me about your bowels. Are your bowels working OK?" Patient: "yeah"; "You're passing urine OK?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah."
Appetite slightly decreased, fluid intake increased: "I've been, I've been drinking a lot more than the usual" and later "maybe a bit less than than what I, I would usually have" regarding eating.

Myalgias for a couple days: doctor summary includes "bit of muscle pain" and earlier ROS: "any general muscle pain or aches, joint pain?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah. Yeah that's, that sort of started in the past couple days."

Patient reports no ongoing medical problems: "are you otherwise fit and well? Or do you have any other medical problems I should be aware of?" Patient: "otherwise that, uh, I'm I'm fine. There isn't anything that I'm taking or, I'm being treated for."
Use of paracetamol and ibuprofen for fever: "I've been taking some Paracetamol and Ibuprofen for that [fever], and they, they help."
No known drug allergies: "any allergies at all to any medications, I should be aware of?" Patient: "Um, no".
Grandmother has type 2 diabetes: "yeah my grandma has diabetes" and when asked type: "I think it's type two."
Great-grandparent with eczema: "one of my uh, great grandads had an eczema."
Lives alone and is an accountant: "I live alone" and "I'm an, I'm an accountant."
Occasional cigar smoking and occasional alcohol: "yeah occasionally, you know, cigars and things on company parties"; alcohol: "occasionally yeah I would have some. I'm, I'm not a very big drinker."

Work stress present but mood okay: patient notes work is "a bit of a stressful period"; when asked if stress affects mood: "no I think I think it's, it's the, you know it's the good kind of stress" and "I like my job."

Doctor’s assessment is viral URTI vs early flu, based on 4-day URI symptoms, myalgias, fatigue, and initial fever: "I think you probably have... a bit of a viral... upper respiratory tract infection, or maybe early signs of a flu." and summary of "since the last four days you've been feeling generally quite unwell, sore throat, runny nose, bit of a dry cough, bit of muscle pain, weakness. Um had initial fever, but now settled."

Headache, night sweats, and decreased appetite are among symptoms of the viral-like illness; though the doctor doesn’t list each explicitly in the summary, all these symptoms are documented in the history and fit a viral syndrome, which the doctor diagnoses as a viral illness/URTI/early flu.
Plan includes rest and increased fluids: "get plenty of rest" and "pushing fluids and make yourself well-hydrated."

Doctor advises continuing paracetamol and ibuprofen: "Continue with the regular Paracetamol, Ibuprofen." While label instructions are not verbatim, continuing as needed per usual use is a direct inference.
Advised to take 1–2 days off work: "I'd probably advise you taking a day or two off work if you can."
Follow-up if not improved by next week: "if next week you're still not better, I'd like you to come back and see me."

Safety net for high fever, worsening breathing, or chest pain: "if you have a high fever, or your breathing is becoming a bit more labored, or chest pain, I'd like you to come back and see me much sooner."
